newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on technical slide, yields.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on technical slide, yields.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on a resumption of a long-term technical slide and on talk soybean yields per acre have been better than expected, traders said.
"Rain in the forecasts firmed the market early but it couldn't hold. This market just cannot go, it cannot hold a rally," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.

Soybeans held firm early on ideas for a slowdown in soybean harvesting due to damp weather overnight in portions of the U.S. Midwest. Also there were showers forecast for later this week in several key U.S. soybean states.
USDA Tuesday said the 1996 U.S. soybean harvest was 40 percent complete, near the low end of trade expectations from 40 to 45 percent and behind the average pace of 52 percent.

Technical factors also were cited with the the nine day relative strength index (RSI) for November closing Wednesday at 18.257 points, below the generally perceived very oversold mark of 20. But technicians pointed out that the four- and 20-day moving averages continued to pressure the November contract, contributing to the longer-term price slippage.
Soybeans closed unchanged to three cents per bushel lower with November down two cents at $6.91.

Traders said the market continued to reel from Friday's bearish USDA crop production report which put this year's U.S. soybean production at 2.346 billion bushels, well above an average pre-report trade estimate for 2.287 billion.
Harvest reports of good to excellent yields in U.S. Midwest early combinings led to talk the USDA may release an even larger estimate in November.
Little direction came from the export sector with the market still perplexed over rumors this week that China had bought or cancelled export orders for U.S. and South American soybeans and soymeal.

Key players included E.D. and F. Man International's sale of two million bushels of January and one million November, traders said. Refco Inc sold 2.5 million November and Paine Webber sold one million November, they said.
Lind Waldock bear spread five million bushels of January/November, the traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 55,000, down from 60,851 Tuesday.

The soybean options pit featured Lind Waldock's purchase of 900 January $7.50 calls, purchase of 900 January $11.00 puts and sale of 900 January $7.50 puts at 3/4 cent, traders said. Refco Inc sold 500 January $7.00 calls at 18-1/4 cents, they said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 23,000, down from 23,843 Tuesday.
